Subject: Capacity check before final MOU — RaptorAI small-batch tiling

Ben / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We captured a lot of optimism on the team side; before legal slots the MOU we need a quick confirmation on the dedicated sizing for our small-batch tiling workload. High level:
- Sustained trial: ~1200 tokens/sec (peak 3000 tokens/sec) for ~8 concurrent POC users.
- Preferred window: Dec 12 — Jan 15 (intensive).
- Requirement: dedicated pool with pre-warm for short bursts; ability to fall back to hosted if our dedicated pool is in maintenance.

Can Redwood provide a firm availability window and any gating questions from infra (slices/nodes/thermal affinity) to avoid last-minute scope changes? If you can send a short capacity spreadsheet we can hand to our procurement & legal.

Jordan

RaptorAI

From: soojin_lee@redwoodai.com
To: ben_carter@redwoodai.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodai.com
Date: Mon, 11 Nov 2029 03:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity check — infra availability for Dec 12 window

Checking infra constraints and copying what I confirmed with the fleet team:

Summary (short):
- We have capacity headroom across our US dedicated pods for Dec 12 — Jan 15 if a soft-commit is placed by 2029-11-12 23:59 PT. Without a soft-commit, we can only promise best-effort and may need to place the account on a shared reserve with slightly higher latency.
- Suggested node mix for the small-batch tiling POC: 6 nodes (A800-equivalent), each node with 4x GPU, continuous KV cache enabled. That meets 1200 sustained tokens/sec with 2x headroom for spikes.
- Pre-warm policy: warm 2 extra nodes 02:00–06:00 UTC for the first 10 days of the window, plus automated 90s burst spin-up for short spikes. There is a measurable cost delta (included in the spreadsheet).
- Maintenance: there are two scheduled maintenance nights for the region (Dec 22 & Jan 7) between 03:00–05:00 UTC. We can add an exemption for RaptorAI on Jan 7 if the legal/commercial team approves a small SLA premium.

Technical caveats and gating questions:
1) Quantization: are you planning 4-bit quant for the tiled models? If yes, memory per KV window drops ~30% and we can fit the same workload on 5 nodes instead of 6. Please confirm model quant profile.
2) Burst profile: define 95th percentile burst length (seconds) and token rate — we assumed 8–12s bursts at 3k tokens/sec.
3) Data residency: confirm whether logs must remain in your VPC (affects telemetry and pre-warm mechanics).

If we get the soft-commit by EOD 2029-11-12 we'll stage the warm nodes in our provisioning queue and lock the slice. If not, we'll offer a conditional fallback (hosted tier with weighted routing) but that will change latency SLOs.

Sooj
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
